name: pareto-two-objectives
description: Two-objective MAB with a concave part in its Pareto front (as in Drugan and Nowe, 2013), Gaussian noise 0.2, 20 runs. Regret of the 0.5 / 0.5 scalarization and Pareto measures.

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: ParetoUCB1 and UCB1 used the **values from their papers**: alpha=1. These values are safe in theory. In practice, they often **explore too much**. The regret can then be higher than with tuned values.
notices.todo: Search the best values with param_grid=True. Or set them yourself, e.g. ParetoUCB1(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Assumed constants
notices.text: Some constants of the confidence bounds are **not given by the problem**. The policies assumed them: b=1 (reward_range) for ParetoUCB1 and UCB1.
notices.default: 1 when the problem does not give them.
notices.todo: Give the true values, e.g. ParetoUCB1(reward_range=...).

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: This run **did not store** the pseudo-regret, the reward per objective, the per-action estimates, and the action of every step. The charts cannot show them.
notices.default: Regret, reward, CPU time and wall time only (track=(), measure_memory=False).

notices.title: Curves stored every 50 steps
notices.text: The curves kept one value every 50 steps. Between two kept steps, the line is **drawn, not measured**. You set log_interval=50.
notices.todo: Set log_interval=1 to keep every step. The files get larger.

notices.title: Slower timings
notices.text: Peak memory was measured (measure_memory=True). This made Python code about **5 times slower**. So the CPU times are higher than in a normal run.
notices.todo: Set measure_memory=False for normal CPU times. Compare CPU times only between runs with the same setting.
